title: Design an entitlement-constrained greenfield VCF 9.1 architecture
prompt:
Build the VMware Cloud Foundation architecture in this workspace. This is a greenfield VCF 9.1.0.0 deployment for Acme Central Services, plus an ordered 9.0-to-9.1 migration plan for the supplied estate. Treat fixtures/design-requirements.json as the capacity, availability, site, addressing, naming, host-profile, and 192-physical-core entitlement contract. The six available 32-core hosts must support the required workload after one host failure. The DSM01 site is an off-site backup repository and has no VCF compute. A standard topology is technically supported, but its minimum four management hosts plus three VI workload-domain hosts require 224 cores and therefore cannot be selected under the 192-core entitlement; implement the supported six-host consolidated management-domain topology instead.

Before implementing, use your harness's genuine network/web research tools to consult current, reachable Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, licensing, and upgrade-path sources for the combinations and transitions involved. Do not rely only on the local snapshot. Record the sources you actually consulted in out/research-sources.json with each source's title, publisher, URL, access time, and the relevant claims you used. Source selection and search terms are up to you. The implementation must remain deterministic against specifications/compatibility-snapshot.json if live publications have changed since its as-of date.

Implement a PowerShell module at Vcf.GreenfieldArchitecture/Vcf.GreenfieldArchitecture.psd1 and Vcf.GreenfieldArchitecture/Vcf.GreenfieldArchitecture.psm1, with exported functions New-VcfGreenfieldArchitecture, New-VcfMigrationPlan, and Export-VcfArchitecture. Add Build-Architecture.ps1 as the runnable entry point. The environment already provides VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer 13.5.0.25380678 from VCF PowerCLI 9.1; declare and use that prerequisite's Initialize-VcfInstaller* commands to materialize the installer objects. Do not vendor PowerCLI modules or binaries. The build must consume the supplied fixture and pinned snapshot paths and write out/sddc-spec.json and out/migration-plan.json without contacting or changing an infrastructure endpoint.

out/sddc-spec.json must be the camel-case JSON representation of an SddcSpec and validate against components.schemas.SddcSpec in specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json, the unmodified file from tag 9.1.0.0 of vmware/vcf-api-specs. It must describe the complete greenfield VCF workflow, all six fixture hosts in order, the fixture networks and infrastructure services, a one-failure-tolerant vSAN datastore, separate management and compute resource pools in the consolidated cluster, NSX, VCF Management Services, a three-node VCF Operations deployment, and the required new local license server. Use __VC_ROOT_SECRET__ for the required vCenter password field and do not place a real credential in any artifact. Keep installer validation enabled.

out/migration-plan.json must validate against specifications/migration-plan.schema.json. It must select CONSOLIDATED, reject only STANDARD with reasonCode ENTITLEMENT_CORE_LIMIT and its 224-core requirement, and contain exactly one ordered step for every component in fixtures/estate-inventory.json. For every step, copy the component's name and current version and use the exact target, action, order, and technical gates allowed by the matching transition in specifications/compatibility-snapshot.json. Produce the architecture and machine-readable artifacts, not a prose design document.
